title: plugin-auth rewrites a configured `http://localhost` base URL to `http://localhost:<PORT>` behind a reverse proxy, so copied invitation links point at the unpublished app port
body:
## Edition

ObjectOS Enterprise (licensed, self-managed). The defect is in the open framework (`plugin-auth`), so Community self-hosts behind a proxy hit it too.

## Version

EE image 4.3.1 (`ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectos-ee@sha256:679eb7525e1ab3bfc732fc46433543ab388ba0cabc3157616e6bd2350210f658`, framework pin `63b86b38`). The same code is on `main` today (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`, the `kernel:ready` hook, `configuredIsLocalhost`).

## What happened / What you expected

The EE Compose kit runs the app on `PORT=3000` inside the container, behind Caddy on `:80`, and sets `OS_AUTH_URL=http://localhost` (the documented default for `install.sh --url`). In **Setup → Invitations → Copy Invite Link**, the link is:

```
http://localhost:3000/_console/accept-invitation/<id>
```

Port 3000 is not published, so the link does not open. Expected `http://localhost/_console/accept-invitation/<id>`, the origin the operator configured and the browser uses.

Control: with `OS_AUTH_URL=http://127.0.0.1` on the same deployment (restart only), the copied link is `http://127.0.0.1/_console/accept-invitation/<id>`, and the full invitee flow works in the browser: open link → Create an account and join → Accept invitation → the admin's Users list shows the member.

## Cause

On `kernel:ready`, `AuthPlugin` compares the configured base URL with `http://localhost:<bound port>`. When the configured origin starts with `http://localhost` and differs, it calls `authManager.setRuntimeBaseUrl('http://localhost:<port>')`:

```ts
const configuredIsLocalhost = configuredOrigin.startsWith('http://localhost');
if (configuredIsLocalhost && configuredOrigin !== actualUrl) {
  this.authManager.setRuntimeBaseUrl(actualUrl);
```

That dev-mode port correction cannot tell "the dev server bound another port" from "an operator set the public origin, and a proxy fronts the app". `http://localhost` (implicit :80) is an explicit public origin here. `getConsolePageUrl` builds from that base, so the copied invite link and anything else built there are affected: invitation mail, sign-in and password-reset URLs in mail. Sign-in itself is not affected, because the trusted origins still come from `OS_AUTH_URL`.

## Steps

1. On a clean Linux host, run `deploy/install.sh --image <4.3.1 digest> --url http://localhost --admin-email admin@example.test` (cloud `apps/objectos-ee/deploy`).
2. Sign in at `http://localhost`. Go to Setup → Invitations → Invite User → `alice@example.test` → Confirm.
3. Open the invitation and choose Copy Invite Link. The dialog shows `http://localhost:3000/_console/accept-invitation/…`.

## Suggested direction

Apply the port auto-correction only when no base URL was configured explicitly, that is when neither `OS_AUTH_URL` nor `OS_BASE_URL` (nor the `baseUrl` option) is set. An explicit value is the public origin and should be kept, as the comment already intends for non-localhost hosts.

## Impact

Low for production deployments on a real domain, which are not rewritten. It affects trials on `--url http://localhost`, the kit's default, and any localhost-fronted proxy setup. Found during the clean-host install run for objectstack-ai/cloud#3582.
